source: due2-native: a binding whose owner states two units (#145)
notes: The policy is valid ODRL 2.2 and passes odrl22-shape.ttl; the rejection is due2's. due2:unit names the one unit of every value read for the operand (decisions/0049 #1), so a binding with two units says nothing about which one a value is in. Two values from different layers would be RetypedOperand, and from two selected modules ConflictingProfileDeclaration; this case states the two units in one graph, the policy's own. Two ranges or two cardinalities are rejected by the same rule, and clingo-i's unit tests cover them.

expected_rejection.why: ex:fee's binding states the euro and the US dollar as its unit. A unit is single-valued, so W1 rejects the binding in stage 2 (due2-profiles.md §3, Checks at normalisation).
